chapters.title: Is it up|and well
narration: These are my server's own dashboards, a row at a time, the way I read them: each row together answers one question. This one is whether file_host is up and well, and where to look first.
They're jsonnet and libsonnet in its repository, built in CI by the image my home server runs, so every panel is in the commit history. The numbers are a made-up week in a throwaway Prometheus.

chapters.title: Mine, or|the load's
narration: Traffic, latency and errors side by side tell me whether a slowdown is my code or the load. In this week a nightly render takes the cores, latency crosses its line, and the server sheds what it can't serve in time.

chapters.title: Asking the|outside
narration: What file_host asks other services, and whether they answered: here an hour of ESPN timing out one morning, and the mailbox missing a few answers late on the last evening.

chapters.title: When the|render runs
narration: The render lane decides when a video may render on four cores without starving what I'm doing: it pauses for interactive work, and holds free memory and pressure against their limits.
These rows lean towards staying up and refusing well, not towards speed yet. When my questions change, new dashboards are one pull request away.
